title: the loop
excerpt: A reflection on how desire changes with our circumstances, and how the thing we chase can give way to what we need right now.
content: we chase dreams based on want.the dream itself becomes secondary somewhere along the way. it turns into a ray. something to follow, not something to reach. far enough that you can keep telling yourself you'll get there. close enough that you don't stop walking.what you actually see most days are the trees blocking the sun.and that's enough. the shade is enough. the tree becomes the thing you were moving toward. not because it was ever the plan, but because it answered what hurt right now.stand in a desert.not thinking about destination. not thinking about purpose. the sun is right above you, sand everywhere, no edge in sight. what do you want? not the dream. not even water first.shade. just shade.the goal collapses. whatever was big becomes small. what's immediate gets louder than what's important.now you're on a boat. ocean everywhere. the thing you were dying for in the desert surrounds you completely. and you still want something. land. out. something that isn't this.desire doesn't stop when it's met. it shifts.and it's not just us. a cloud passes over a bird for a few seconds. that's enough. a human sits under the same tree for an hour. we carry desire longer. we build stories around it. we call it a dream and give it a name.but the mechanism is the same. the want arrives. it narrows everything down to the most urgent version of itself. you move toward it. and once it's close enough. something else surfaces.the loop doesn't end.it just changes what it's looping around.maybe that's not a flaw. maybe the loop was always the point.

title: My Thoughts on Dark Matter
imageAlt: Cover of Dark Matter by Blake Crouch
excerpt: A review of Blake Crouch’s novel, its approachable science, and the quiet emotional weight of choices and lives not lived.
content: i just finished dark matter.worth every page. i say this as someone who reads slowly, carefully, the kind of reader who notices when the writing is working too hard to impress you.this one doesnt do that.the language sits above casual reading. the grammar, the words used, the way sentences are constructed. if you havent read much fiction it might slow you down in the beginning. but i can tell you this. at no point while reading it did i feel bored or lost. the story pulls. you stop noticing the language and start seeing it. like watching a sci-fi film behind your eyes.what surprised me most is how the science is handled. there are complicated references. quantum mechanics, multiverse theory, things that sound like they belong in a textbook. but blake crouch never drops them on you and walks away. the explanation always comes with the scene. you dont need to google anything. the book explains itself.and the emotions. every page had something that landed. not because it was written dramatically but because it was written honestly. nothing felt like it was there to fill space.the characters are developed well. jason's world, the people in it, their roles in his story are written without overcomplication. even the parallel jasons, which could have easily become confusing, never did. you always knew where you were.ryan holder. leighton. amanda. the other versions of daniela, the other versions of jason. some of them are there for very little time. but each one matters. none of them feel decorative.the scene i keep coming back to is jason at daniela's house. early in the book. he is sitting across from her knowing this isnt his world, knowing she doesnt know him the way his daniela does. and instead of shutting down the conversation she asks him questions. what does your life look like. how is charlie. what does he look like.and the way he answers her. the way he describes his son to a woman who in another life is the mother of that son. that scene does something to you quietly. it doesnt announce itself. it just sits there and tells you everything about what choices cost.that is what this book is really about.not parallel universes. not the science.choices. the weight of them. the fact that every door you walk through closes another one. and you will always wonder. and you will always lose something. and that is not a flaw in how life works. that is just what life is.the book ends with one idea that i am still thinking about. reality is the only truth that cannot be changed. you can question yourself. your personality will shift. the person you were at twenty will not be the person you are at thirty. but the present moment, this one, right now, is the only thing that is actually real. and you have to learn to own it. not mourn the versions of yourself you left behind. not chase the ones you never became.just own where you are.i think about that a lot.
